newsitem.title: UK: Dollar pauses for breath after steep climb.
newsitem.headline: Dollar pauses for breath after steep climb.

text.p: The dollar, reinvigorated by favourable comments from finance ministers of the G7 industrialised countries, climbed steeply early on Monday before pausing for breath in later trading.

On European equity markets, a lacklustre session was not helped by an unsettled start on Wall Street though London and Paris managed to edge ahead in trading that was dominated by upcoming general elections.

The dollar surged in early trade to a 37-month high against the mark and near its 55-month peak against the yen before easing in early afternoon as the bullish mood created by Sunday's G7 meeting cooled .
But traders said a pause was only natural after the dollar's sprint forward.
"The dollar's been well-bid all morning. Most people think this is a reasonable level to buy dollars after the G7 made them feel quite comfortable about buying it," said one trader at a British bank.
The dollar soared after the G7 ministers said major currency misalignments had been corrected and that excessive currency volatility and deviations from fundamentals were undesirable.
Analysts said the remarks lacked aggressiveness and had made dollar bulls comfortable. Traders will test the central banks' resolve by bidding the dollar up gradually, they added.

"For this week at least the forex market will be a bit nervous but assuming no intervention comes through I think we will be back to seeing people becoming reasonably bullish on the dollar again," said Stephen King, International Economist at HSBC James Capel.
Forex traders say continued verbal intervention will have little or no impact and only a dose of actual central bank dollar selling will calm the dollar bulls down.

"Jawboning isn't enough, only intervention will stop it in the short-term," said one trader at a leading U.S. bank. "And there is a big enough question mark over possible intervention to keep the dollar bulls happy."

The dollar, which climbed one-and-a-half pfennigs in overnight deals, eased to 1.7285 marks in afternoon trade, compared to the 1.7235 in late European trade on Friday. It was at 126.55 yen, off a peak of 127.10 but still well up from its pre-G7 Friday level of 125.92.
A factor clouding the markets was a warning from the G7 ministers on trade imbalances.

They stressed the importance of avoiding currency moves that could lead to a re-emergence of large trade imbalances. They named no names, but markets saw this as a reference to Japan's swelling, politically sensitive trade surplus with the U.S.

In equity markets, French stocks made the healthiest gains, moving ahead 0.34 percent with investors taking comfort from two polls giving the ruling centre-right coalition a sizeable majority in the upcoming parliamentary election.

A poll published in Monday's Le Figaro saw the centre-right winning the May 25-June 1 election with 329 seats, with the Socialists, other left and ecologists obtaining 202. Another poll published on Sunday also showed the RPR-UDF coalition and conservative allies winning.
The two polls provided some reassurance for the French financial markets, which were jolted last week by a poll predicting a tight race.

London shares moved ahead only a few points, with the market unsettled by political uncertainty over the outcome of Thursday's UK election and New York stocks, which lost 0.41 percent shortly after the opening on Monday.
Dealers also said markets were likely fret over U.S. figures this week -- culminating in the key employment report on Friday -- which could renew fears of a rise in U.S. interest rates.

In Frankfurt, the picture was mixed with floor trade ending down 0.33 percent but deals on the computerised IBIS index making modest gains, boosted by the stronger dollar and improved dollar prospects.
STOCKS AT 1430 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was up 6.6 points at 4,376.3.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 13.75 points at 2,549.99.
Frankfurt's DAX index ended down 11.04 points at 3363.06.
CURRENCIES AT 1430 GMT
The dollar stood at 1.7285 against the mark versus 1.7235 in late European trade on Friday. Against the yen, the dollar was quoted at 126.55 from 125.92.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was in the afternoon at $340.20 an ounce after ending at $342.45 in London on Friday. Silver was at $4.64, down nine points.
